turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come in, please, that chair is free. What brings the two of you this morning?
[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, I have brought my husband. He will say he is absolutely fine, but I am worried sick.
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): I am fine only. Why she has dragged me, I don't understand. Your downstairs waiting room was packed, we sat there forty minutes.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry about that wait. Madam, in your own words, what have you actually noticed?
[SEG0005] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It has been six months... um, no, six is wrong. Four months, after Diwali. He asks the same question again and again, sometimes three times in ten minutes.
[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): I do not repeat questions. If she is in the kitchen she doesn't hear, so I ask once more, that is all. Are you going to write mad in the file?
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am writing both versions, nothing else. What about his appointments?
[SEG0008] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He forgot the dentist last Tuesday, and the eye check the week before. I had told him that morning, and it was on the calendar also.
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): I did not forget the dentist. I cancelled, the tooth itself was not paining. The eye people had shifted their room. Why is everyone assuming I am forgetful?
[SEG0010] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And he got lost, doctor. Last month, from the sabzi market, he phoned and said he cannot find our lane. The neighbour uncle walked him to the gate of our flat.
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): I was not lost. The auto stand was empty, so I took the temple road, which is longer, that is all. Will you send me to a mental hospital for this? Tell me straight.

[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): No admission and no mental hospital. Let me say it back. Your wife says that for four months you repeat questions, that two appointments were missed, and that last month you could not find the lane. You say you only asked again when she didn't hear, you cancelled the dentist, and you chose a longer road.
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): That summary is kinder to her than to me. I am seventy-four, not ninety. Sometimes a name slips, whose doesn't? Otherwise my memory is perfectly ok.
[SEG0014] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And the building accounts, doctor. Twice the secretary had to redo his figures. He still thinks he did them right.

[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): That secretary is new, he cannot read my handwriting. It is not my memory. If you write memory problem, will the RTO cancel my driving? I have to reach the temple on Thursdays.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am not writing to the RTO, and I am not stopping your driving today. Any falls, blackouts, fits, or weakness on one side?
[SEG0017] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): None of that. No fall. He still walks to the market every morning, quite steady.
[SEG0018] person_3 (PATIENT): Exactly. No blackout, no fit, nothing like that. Why ask stroke things? Do you already think it is a stroke? Should I be scared?
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): From what you both describe, this is not how a stroke presents. I am not naming any illness. How is sleep, and how is his mood?
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): Sleep is good. I get up once for the bathroom and then I am off again. I am not sad. I am only tense because she forced this visit. Does tension also go in the notes?
[SEG0021] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sleep is mostly fine, yes. Mood-wise he is irritable. If I remind him of anything he snaps. He will say that is not true.
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): I snap because she nags, not because my mood is ill. There is a difference, no? How long is this consultation, I need to pass urine soon.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): We are about halfway. Who gives the medicines at home?
[SEG0024] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I do, all of them. If I leave the box with him, doses get missed, so I put each tablet in his hand myself.
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): She hides the strips like I am a schoolboy. I know what I take, one for BP and one for cholesterol. I am not careless.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Madam, the names and the doses you actually give, please.

[SEG0027] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Amlodipine for the pressure, ten milligrams... ah, sorry, that was the old dose. It is five milligrams now, one tablet in the morning after breakfast. Atorvastatin twenty milligrams at night. Vitamin D, sixty thousand units, one capsule every Sunday.

[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): Don't add any sugar tablet. Metformin is my elder sister's, for her sugar, not mine. Once the strips got mixed at her house and everyone panicked. I have no sugar disease.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Metformin stays off his list. Any allergy to a drug or a food, sir?
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): No. No allergy. I have told this in every OPD. I can eat everything.

[SEG0031] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I don't agree. Some fifteen years back an antibiotic, I am quite sure it was amoxicillin, brought out red itchy patches. We stopped it and the patches went. He denies it every single time.

[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): That was the May heat, doctor, not the capsule. If a nurse gives me amoxicillin tomorrow, will my throat close? Should I carry a paper in my wallet? I am really getting anxious.

[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): I will note that you deny any allergy and your wife recalls a possible amoxicillin rash. We will avoid amoxicillin until it is clearer. I cannot say what a dose would do, because the story is not settled.

[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): Fine. Since you want old history, at a camp they checked my thyroid. Two years back... well, actually it may be three, I can't place it. They said borderline. No number, just borderline. I never took a thyroid tablet.

[SEG0035] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes, the free camp near the Ganesh temple. They said repeat it, we never did. He has had no operation in his life. Cataract was mentioned, both eyes, they said it can wait, so nothing was done.

[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): So an old camp thyroid test, called borderline, not repeated, and no thyroid medicine. No surgery. Cataract left to wait. The BP and the cholesterol are still ongoing, yes?

[SEG0037] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes. BP from my fifties, still there. Cholesterol they picked up some years later, also still there. Is borderline thyroid a cancer? My neighbour had a thyroid operation. I don't want anyone cutting my neck.
[SEG0038] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Also, his mother had memory loss in her last years. The family just said old age. No doctor put a name on it. I should have said that earlier.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Noted, that is his mother's history, not a label for him. Hearing about the market episode, I was going to book a CT scan of the head today.

[SEG0040] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He already had a head CT, eight years ago, after he slipped from a scooter. They said the scan was normal. He panics inside those machines. And last week the pharmacy machine read one seventy over ninety-six. He refused to recheck.

[SEG0041] person_3 (PATIENT): That pharmacy machine always shows high. At home it is one thirty or something, I don't remember the exact figure. I am not entering any CT. What is the cost? A blood test is enough, no? I already had tea, does that spoil it?

[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): The earlier CT was reported normal, and you don't want the machine, so I am dropping the scan. I have changed my mind on that. We will do bloods instead, blood count, sugar, kidney, liver, thyroid, B12 and cholesterol, and I will arrange a memory assessment at the specialist clinic. No memory tablet, and no diagnosis from me today.
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): Memory assessment means a test, like school? If I forget one answer, do I fail? Will they then say Alzheimer's? Please, I need to know. And is tomorrow fasting?

[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): It is a clinic assessment, not a pass or fail, and I am not saying Alzheimer's or any other name. For the bloods, come fasting tomorrow, only water from tonight. Take the morning tablets with a sip of water, don't skip them.
[SEG0045] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I will bring him around eight. The Sunday vitamin D is still due. Should I hold it?
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): No, give the vitamin D on Sunday as usual. Amlodipine five milligrams every morning, atorvastatin twenty at night, all of them continue.
[SEG0047] person_3 (PATIENT): My wife's cousin swallows some memory capsule from America, very costly. If your tests take time, shall we just buy it, to be on the safe side?
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Please don't. That capsule is not his, and I have nothing to treat yet. Starting it on your own will only confuse the picture.
[SEG0049] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): One more thing. This week he misplaced his spectacles twice, then said I had hidden them in the kitchen.
[SEG0050] person_3 (PATIENT): You had kept them in the kitchen, I found them there. That is not misplacing. If the blood test comes normal, then what? Do we still come, or is the file closed?

[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): Even if the bloods are normal, the memory assessment still goes ahead. Either way I want both of you back here in about two weeks, with the reports. The clinic date may fall a little after that.
[SEG0052] person_3 (PATIENT): Two weeks feels long if something is serious. What should make us rush? I keep imagining the worst, I can't help it.
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): If he becomes suddenly much more confused, or weak in one arm or leg, or gets a severe headache, go to emergency that same day. Don't wait for my clinic.
[SEG0054] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I understand. He still walks to the market alone. Should I stop that from today?
[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes. Until the assessment is done, he should not go out alone. Someone should accompany him. It is a precaution, not a final word on his independence.

[SEG0056] person_3 (PATIENT): So the market is also banned? This feels like house arrest. You said no admission, but listen to all these rules. Will the memory people come to this room, or must we travel?

[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): You will go to their outpatient clinic. My staff will book the slot and call you. You are not being admitted. I have both stories, and they don't match on several points, which is why the assessment will help. Any last question?
[SEG0058] person_3 (PATIENT): Only this. You are sure you have no name for it today? Not even a small possible name?
[SEG0059] person_1 (DOCTOR): No name today. We will talk again when the blood reports and the memory assessment are in front of us. Go home safely, both of you.

features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.

third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.

bad.reason: Patient mentions elder sister has sugar; family history relation is supported, condition wording differs.
